Published 2026-11-15. ISO/IEC 42001, published in December 2023, sets requirements for an AI management system and can be certified by an accredited body. It follows the familiar ISO clause structure and adds 38 reference controls in Annex A. A companion standard for certification bodies, ISO/IEC 42006, followed in July 2025, and UKAS accredited its first certifier in January 2026.

## [What Is Lead Scoring?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-lead-scoring/)

Published 2026-11-15. Lead scoring assigns points to leads for fit and engagement so sales can prioritise. Modern CRMs offer rules-based and predictive versions, but Forrester argues that scoring individuals misses how B2B buying groups actually decide. This explainer covers how lead scores are built, what predictive scoring needs, and how to check whether a score works.

## [What Is Lead Source Attribution?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-lead-source-attribution/)

Published 2026-11-15. Lead source attribution assigns each lead, and the revenue that follows, to the channel that produced it. It is one of the most used fields in a CRM and one of the least reliable, because most B2B buying happens before a buyer is visible. This explainer covers how the field works in common CRMs, the main attribution approaches, and a setup a mid-size firm can trust.

## [What Is LLM Observability?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-llm-observability/)

Published 2026-11-15. LLM observability extends application monitoring to systems whose outputs vary from run to run. It rests on traces of each request, cost and latency data, and evaluations of quality. OpenTelemetry is standardising the format, but the conventions are still in development.

## [What Is MEDDICC?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-meddicc/)

Published 2026-11-15. MEDDICC is a checklist for qualifying complex B2B deals, built around the evidence a seller needs before a forecast can be trusted. It began at PTC in the 1990s and has since gained letters for competition and the paper process. This explainer sets out what each element means, why it suits buying groups of a dozen or more people, and how to turn it into CRM fields rather than a training slide.

## [What Is Model Drift?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-model-drift/)

Published 2026-11-15. Model drift is the gradual or sudden change in how an AI system performs after it goes live. Classic drift comes from the world changing under a trained model. With hosted language models there is a second cause: the provider changes or retires the model. Both are caught the same way, by re-running fixed tests on a schedule.

## [What Is Model Risk Management for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-model-risk-management/)

Published 2026-11-15. Model risk management covers the inventory, development, validation, monitoring and governance of models whose errors could cause loss. In April 2026 US banking agencies rescinded SR 11-7 and issued principles-based guidance, SR 26-2, which explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI. The UK PRA's SS1/23 still covers AI used in modelling. For firms outside banking, the discipline is a useful template for AI tools that drive decisions.

## [What Is Net Revenue Retention (NRR)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-net-revenue-retention/)

Published 2026-11-15. Net revenue retention measures whether a firm's existing customers are worth more or less to it than they were a year ago. Above 100% means expansion outweighs losses; below it means the firm must replace revenue before it can grow. This explainer gives the formula, recent benchmarks for private software companies, and the measurement errors that most often inflate the figure.

## [What Is Outcome-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-outcome-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-15. Outcome-based pricing charges for a measured result rather than for access or volume. Customer-service AI vendors have led, charging per resolution. It aligns cost with value only when both sides can measure and trust the result, so the buyer's main task is to read, test and audit the vendor's definition of an outcome.

## [What Is Outcome Write-Back?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-outcome-write-back/)

Published 2026-11-15. Outcome write-back is the step that records what happened after a decision against the decision itself, in the system the next decision will read. It is the learning stage of the enterprise brain. The plumbing to move data back into a CRM already exists; what is usually missing is a decision to attach the outcome to.

## [What Is Permission-Aware Retrieval?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-permission-aware-retrieval/)

Published 2026-11-15. Permission-aware retrieval filters what an AI assistant or agent can retrieve to what the requesting person is allowed to open in the source system. It is the standard design for enterprise assistants. It inherits every overshared file and lags behind permission changes, so commercial content should be audited and tested with restricted users before it is connected.

## [What Is Pipeline Coverage?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-pipeline-coverage/)

Published 2026-11-15. Pipeline coverage compares the value of open opportunities with the revenue still to be won in a period. The familiar 3x rule only holds at a one-in-three win rate, so firms that copy it often plan with too little or too much pipeline. This explainer sets out the formula, how to derive your own ratio from win rate and cycle length, and how to stop coverage being inflated by deals that will never close.

## [What Is Product-Led Growth?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-product-led-growth/)

Published 2026-11-15. Product-led growth is a go-to-market motion in which people find, try and start paying for a product largely on their own, with sales joining later to expand accounts. Investor benchmarks show it can grow fast but converts only a small share of free users. It fits products that deliver value without a conversation, and breaks when setup, integration or a buying committee stands in the way.

## [What Is Prompt Caching?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-caching/)

Published 2026-11-15. Prompt caching stores the processed form of a prompt's fixed opening, such as instructions, tools or a policy document, so later requests that start the same way skip that work. Cache hits are billed at a fraction of the input price and answers start sooner; output is unchanged. The saving depends on prompt order and on keeping the fixed part identical.

## [What Is Prompt Engineering?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-engineering/)

Published 2026-11-15. Prompt engineering is the practice of writing, structuring and testing the instructions an AI model works from. Research shows formatting alone can move accuracy by up to 76 points, so a prompt is only as reliable as the tests run against it. It fixes wording and format; facts, permissions and rules belong in context and code.

## [What Is Prompt Injection?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-injection/)

Published 2026-11-15. Prompt injection is the leading risk in OWASP's 2025 list for LLM applications. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre warns it may never be fully mitigated, because language models do not separate instructions from data. The practical answer is design: limit what an agent can reach and require a person before anything leaves the company.

## [What Is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retrieval-augmented-generation/)

Published 2026-11-15. Retrieval-augmented generation is a technique where an AI system searches a knowledge base for relevant passages and adds them to the model's input before it answers. It grounds responses in your own documents, but it does not eliminate errors: a Stanford study found RAG-based legal tools still hallucinated on more than 17% of queries. Retrieval quality, source freshness and citations decide whether it works.

## [What Is Revenue Intelligence?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-revenue-intelligence/)

Published 2026-11-15. Revenue intelligence software captures sales activity from email, calendars and calls, joins it to CRM data and uses it to score deals, flag risk and support forecasts. In December 2025 Gartner folded the category into a wider market it calls revenue action orchestration. The evaluation questions are what activity it captures, whether its scores can be checked against outcomes, and what it is allowed to do without a person.

## [What Is Revenue Operations (RevOps)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-revenue-operations/)

Published 2026-11-15. Revenue operations joins the operational work behind marketing, sales and customer success into one function with one set of definitions and one data model. Analysts have tracked it for years, and it matters more now that AI agents read the same records. This explainer covers what RevOps is, what it owns, and how a 20 to 500 person firm can start.

## [What Is Reverse ETL?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-reverse-etl/)

Published 2026-11-15. Reverse ETL moves data out of the warehouse and into operational tools such as the CRM, so scores and usage figures appear where sellers and agents work. The category is consolidating into wider data movement platforms. The main risk is not technical: it is a sync overwriting fields that people own.

## [What Is Robotic Process Automation (RPA) in the Age of Agents?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-robotic-process-automation/)

Published 2026-11-15. Robotic process automation uses software robots to repeat a person's actions on screen, which makes it useful for legacy systems with no API. Vendors now position RPA robots as the deterministic executors inside agentic automation, with agents handling judgment and people approving. The practical order is API first, RPA for legacy screens, and an agent only where a decision is needed.

## [What Is Sales Forecasting, and Why Is It Usually Wrong?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-forecasting/)

Published 2026-11-15. A sales forecast predicts what will close in a period, usually by combining pipeline data with seller and manager judgment. Gartner found fewer than half of sales leaders and sellers have high confidence in their forecast. This explainer covers the main forecasting methods, the structural reasons forecasts miss, and how a mid-size firm can measure and reduce its error.

## [What Is Sales Velocity?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-velocity/)

Published 2026-11-15. Sales velocity turns four pipeline measures into one figure: revenue produced per day. Its value is diagnostic, because it shows which of the four levers is moving and by how much. This explainer gives the formula and a worked example, explains why recent benchmark data shows all four levers under pressure, and sets out how a mid-size team can use it without gaming it.

## [What Is Seat-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-seat-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-15. Seat-based pricing charges per named user per month, as most AI assistants do. It is predictable, but seats now come with usage limits and metered extras, and agents weaken the link between users and value. Gartner and Deloitte both expect hybrid pricing to spread. Buyers should size seats to a workflow, read the usage terms and track weekly use per seat.

## [What Is Selling Time, and Why Do Sellers Spend So Little of It Selling?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-seller-time-to-sell/)

Published 2026-11-15. Selling time is the share of a seller's working week spent engaging prospects and clients. Salesforce's surveys have put it between roughly 30% and 40% for years, with the rest lost to administration, internal meetings and data entry. This explainer defines the measure, explains where time goes, and sets out how to recover it without simply adding tools.

## [What Is Shadow AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-shadow-ai/)

Published 2026-11-15. Shadow AI is the use of AI tools at work without the organisation's approval or oversight. Surveys suggest it is the norm rather than the exception, and IBM-sponsored research links it to costlier breaches. Bans rarely work; an approved alternative, a short policy and an inventory do.

## [What Is Structured Output in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-structured-output/)

Published 2026-11-15. Structured output constrains an AI model's response to a schema the developer supplies, so it parses and contains the required fields. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google all enforce schemas during generation. The guarantee covers shape, not truth: values still need checking before anything acts on them.

## [What Is Synthetic Data?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-synthetic-data/)

Published 2026-11-15. Synthetic data is artificial data generated by algorithms to reproduce the statistical patterns of real data. It is useful for testing, for training where data is scarce, and for sharing without exposing records. The ICO warns it can still be personal data, and research in Nature shows models trained recursively on generated data degrade.

## [What Are TAM, SAM and SOM?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-tam-sam-som/)

Published 2026-11-15. TAM, SAM and SOM describe a market at three levels: everything that could be bought, the part a firm can serve, and the share it can realistically win. The numbers are only as good as the market definition behind them, as a public 2014 dispute over Uber's valuation showed. This explainer defines the three terms, compares top-down and bottom-up methods, and sets out how a 20 to 500 person firm can build a SOM its sales team recognises.

## [What Is the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-agent2agent-protocol/)

Published 2026-11-15. The Agent2Agent protocol is an open standard, launched by Google in April 2025 and now hosted by the Linux Foundation, that lets AI agents built on different platforms delegate tasks to each other. It complements MCP, which connects an agent to tools and data. By April 2026 more than 150 organisations supported it, but cross-vendor delegation raises questions of accountability that the protocol alone does not answer.

## [What Is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-model-context-protocol/)

Published 2026-11-15. The Model Context Protocol is an open standard, released by Anthropic in November 2024, that lets AI applications connect to tools and data through one common interface instead of custom integrations. By December 2025 it had more than 10,000 active public servers and was donated to a Linux Foundation fund. It is wiring: useful to rent, but it needs permissions and logging around it.

## [What Is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-nist-ai-risk-management-framework/)

Published 2026-11-15. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is voluntary guidance, released in January 2023, that organises AI risk work into four functions: govern, map, measure and manage. A Generative AI Profile followed in July 2024, and NIST says the framework is being revised. For a mid-size firm it is most useful as a structure for an AI inventory and a review routine, not as a certification.

## [What Is Usage-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-usage-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-15. Usage-based pricing charges for the volume of AI work done rather than the number of users. Major vendors have moved agent products to credits and per-action rates, and hybrids of a platform fee plus usage are becoming the norm. Buyers should insist on caps, estimates and alerts, and know what one completed task costs.

## [What Is Value-Based Pricing?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-value-based-pricing/)

Published 2026-11-15. Value-based pricing sets a price from the value an offer creates for a defined buyer, measured against that buyer's next best alternative. Pricing research treats it as the strongest approach and finds it the least used. The difficulty is less the arithmetic than measuring value, segmenting by it and holding the price once sellers start to negotiate.

## [What Is Win-Loss Analysis?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-win-loss-analysis/)

Published 2026-11-15. Win-loss analysis asks buyers, not just sellers, why a deal went the way it did. Research suggests seller-recorded reasons often differ from what buyers report, and that many losses are to no decision rather than a competitor. This explainer covers what win-loss analysis is, how a programme works, and how a mid-size firm can run a first round.

## [What Is Zero Data Retention in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-zero-data-retention/)

Published 2026-11-15. Zero data retention is an arrangement under which an AI provider keeps no prompts or outputs at rest once a response is returned. It is approved per customer, covers only eligible endpoints, and keeps exceptions for flagged content and legal holds. In 2026 providers began limiting it for their most capable models, so buyers should check retention per model and per feature.

## [What We Would Cut From the Build Order](https://lowob.com/research/what-we-would-cut-from-the-build-order/)

Published 2026-11-15. After thirteen parts, a retrospective. The evidence on AI project failure points more often to over-building than under-building: RAND's interviews name chasing technology over the problem as a leading cause, and Anthropic's own guidance is to find the simplest solution that works. For firms under about 50 people, several steps in The Build Order shrink to a habit or disappear. Four do not: a named owner, one recorded decision class, nothing sends without a person, and a handover that keeps the reasoning.

## [Which AI Assistant, Which Seats](https://lowob.com/research/which-ai-assistant-which-seats/)

Published 2026-11-15. The model is the fastest-changing and least sticky layer of the stack. Choose an assistant by suite fit, connector depth and open-standard support, administrative and data controls, and whether outputs and approvals can be logged. Buy seats for the people in the first workflow, not the whole company.

## [Why the Brain Starts at the Commercial Line](https://lowob.com/research/why-the-brain-starts-at-the-commercial-line/)

Published 2026-11-15. Commercial decisions are frequent, similar, graded within a quarter and defended by a budget holder, and they sit on the most structured data most firms own. Firm-wide knowledge bases are the most requested starting point and the hardest to justify a year later. Regulated sectors and long sales cycles change the order.

## [Running a Win-Loss Programme](https://lowob.com/research/win-loss-programmes/)

Published 2026-11-15. Most firms have tried win-loss once. Few run it as a programme, and the evidence suggests seller-recorded loss reasons rarely match what buyers say. This piece sets out the design choices that keep a programme alive past its first report: a sampling rule, a neutral interviewer, a fixed coding frame, and a route from each theme to a named owner and a recorded decision.

## [Workflow Automation vs AI Agents: Which Do You Need?](https://lowob.com/research/workflow-automation-vs-ai-agents/)

Published 2026-11-15. Workflow automation follows a path designed in advance; an AI agent decides its next step at run time. Anthropic and OpenAI both advise starting with the simplest option, and Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by 2027. Most commercial processes need a workflow with a model step inside it, and an agent only where judgment or unstructured input dominates.

## [Your CRM Is Memory, Not a Brain](https://lowob.com/research/your-crm-is-memory-not-a-brain/)

Published 2026-11-15. The CRM is the store layer of the brain: necessary, not sufficient. Most CRM data is not ready for AI, and agents now act on its errors automatically. The fix is a short list of fields the brain needs, a time-boxed clean-up, automatic capture of activity, and a required reason for every lost deal.

## [The 10 crypto events worth the trip, Nov 2026–Jul 2027](https://lowob.com/research/the-10-crypto-events-worth-the-trip-nov-2026-jul-2027/)

Published 2026-10-26. Consensus Miami (4–6 May 2027) ranks first among crypto events worth flying to between November 2026 and July 2027, followed by Devcon 8 and EthCC[10]. The ranking reflects where deals get done for companies selling into crypto, not attendance.

## [Top 10 applied-AI events, Nov 2026–Jun 2027](https://lowob.com/research/top-10-applied-ai-events-nov-2026-jun-2027/)

Published 2026-10-26. Vendor shows are where AI roadmaps are announced, while analyst and finance-specific events are where peers in regulated firms compare what works, so a balanced year includes one of each. Gartner Data & Analytics Summit (8–10 Mar 2027, Orlando) ranks first, followed by Money20/20 Europe and AWS re:Invent.

## [Five invariants, from two people to ten thousand](https://lowob.com/research/five-invariants-from-two-people-to-ten-thousand/)

Published 2026-10-23. Almost everything about an enterprise brain changes with size, but five things do not: decisions recorded with a reason and falsifier, sources kept, views superseded rather than overwritten, outcomes written back, and an organisation-owned record. Each has an established precedent outside AI. They cost almost nothing at two people and are the hardest thing to retrofit at ten thousand.

## [The 5 enterprise context platforms, ranked for regulated firms](https://lowob.com/research/the-5-enterprise-context-platforms-ranked-for-regulated-firms/)

Published 2026-10-23. Every vendor now calls this layer an enterprise brain; what they sell is a context layer that connects documents, data and permissions to agents. For a regulated firm the deciding questions are whether permissions follow the user, whether you can reconstruct what an agent saw and did, and whether you can leave. Glean ranks first, then Microsoft Work IQ, Google Gemini Enterprise, Writer and Dust.

## [Top 5 AI governance and audit-trail tools](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-governance-and-audit-trail-tools/)

Published 2026-10-23. AI governance platforms became a real category in 2026, when Gartner published its first Magic Quadrant for them in June. For banks and insurers, the platforms differ most on whether they map explicitly to model-risk guidance; most map to the EU AI Act and NIST and leave bank supervision implicit. This ranking verifies each vendor's analyst standing, features and prices as listed in November 2026.

## [The 10 AI regulatory dates to watch through 2027](https://lowob.com/research/the-10-ai-regulatory-dates-to-watch-through-2027/)

Published 2026-10-22. The AI-specific rules keep slipping, but the record-keeping, supervision and resilience rules that already apply do not. Refreshed in November 2026, this list covers the ten dates that change what a financial firm in the US, UK or EU must do or show, and what happened to the ones that have passed. Every date points to the same need: a record you can reconstruct.

## [The transitions that break the brain](https://lowob.com/research/the-transitions-that-break-the-brain/)

Published 2026-10-22. Organisations rarely lose their reasoning gradually; they lose it at transitions such as the first hire, an acquisition, a founder's departure or a platform migration. Each is predictable and has a specific defence, and the defence is always cheaper before the transition than after it. Regulation and standard practice already describe several of the defences.

## [Top 5 AI customer-service agents, by pricing model](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-customer-service-agents-by-pricing-model/)

Published 2026-10-22. Customer service is the one place outcome pricing has taken hold, because a resolved ticket can be counted, so the definition of "resolved" is the most important line in the contract. The ranking is Fin, Zendesk AI agents, Sierra, Salesforce Agentforce and Decagon, with prices as listed in November 2026.

## [Top 5 AI notetakers for decision capture](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-notetakers-for-decision-capture/)

Published 2026-10-21. Every notetaker now transcribes well; the difference is whether it helps you capture what was decided and why, whether you own and can export the record, and whether everyone knew they were recorded. Granola ranks first, then Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Circleback and Google Meet with Gemini notes, with prices as listed in November 2026.

## [Top 5 tools for a founders' decision ledger](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-tools-for-a-founders-decision-ledger/)

Published 2026-10-21. None of these tools is truly append-only; every one lets someone edit an old entry. The ranking is Notion, Slite, Airtable, Obsidian and Tana, judged on version history, open export, ease of the weekly habit, and AI drafting and price as listed in November 2026. A shared document with a weekly review beats a perfect database nobody opens.

## [Buy Context. Own Judgment. What Enterprise AI Teams Should Build](https://lowob.com/research/buy-context-own-judgment-what-to-build-at-each-size/)

Published 2026-10-20. At every company size, rent the context layer as it matures and own the record of how you decide. Most enterprises now buy rather than build their AI, which makes the decision record, and the right to take it with you, the part to control. What 'own' means grows from a document and a habit at two people to a governed service at ten thousand.

## [The financial data providers your agents can call today](https://lowob.com/research/the-financial-data-providers-your-agents-can-call-today/)

Published 2026-10-20. In about twelve months every major financial data provider adopted the same agent connection protocol, MCP, so agents can call licensed data from inside Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and the cloud marketplaces. FactSet ranks first because it is the only one that quantifies AI's share of growth; the others differ on disclosure, entitlements and how clearly they price.

## [Top 5 LLM observability and evaluation platforms](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-llm-observability-and-evaluation-platforms/)

Published 2026-10-20. The top five LLM observability and evaluation platforms, ranked for regulated teams, are Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize, Braintrust and Datadog. The deciding questions are whether you can self-host, whether it supports OpenTelemetry so you are not locked in, and whether human review is logged alongside traces. This guide compares them side by side, prices them at production volume and sets out where the OpenTelemetry standard stands.

## [Ten thousand people: density, and the case for federation](https://lowob.com/research/ten-thousand-people-density-and-the-case-for-federation/)

Published 2026-10-19. At ten thousand people, an enterprise has enough volume across decision classes for a learning layer to earn its keep. A single unified enterprise brain tends to stall; the workable design is federated: central invariants and one export format, records and local definitions kept by functions, and a map between them. Data architecture reached the same design under the name data mesh.

## [The 5 agent memory layers worth testing, and how to test them](https://lowob.com/research/the-5-agent-memory-layers-worth-testing-and-how-to-test-them/)

Published 2026-10-19. No memory layer has yet shown, under independent test, that it makes agents better at long tasks, and the hardest case, a fact that has changed, is where every system tested so far is weakest. Zep, Mem0, Letta, Cognee and Supermemory are worth testing, ranked mainly on how they handle change over time. Run your own two-week test rather than trust vendor scores.

## [Top 5 agent frameworks for production, by state model and cloud](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-agent-frameworks-for-production-by-state-model-and-cloud/)

Published 2026-10-19. Framework choice in 2026 is mostly a cloud and vendor decision, because the serious options now share the same tool protocol. For a regulated team the differences are whether a run can pause for a human, resume after a crash and run on more than one model. LangGraph ranks first, followed by Microsoft Agent Framework, the Claude Agent SDK, Google's ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

## [One thousand people: governance arrives](https://lowob.com/research/one-thousand-people-governance-arrives/)

Published 2026-10-15. At around a thousand people, auditors, regulators, security teams and large customers start asking how decisions were made, and "we discussed it" stops being an answer. The record's job becomes governance: a trace specification, an evidenced review gate, registered agents and agreed retention. Each decision record should be owned by the business function whose decisions it records.

## [The Enterprise Brain Is a Record, Not a Mind](https://lowob.com/research/the-enterprise-brain-is-a-record-not-a-mind/)

Published 2026-10-15. Every 'enterprise brain' product on the market is the same three things: memory, meaning and governance. That is a real context layer, but not a brain, because nobody has shipped the fourth layer, judgment: how the organisation decides. The brain that compounds is a record of decisions that can be audited and revised.

## [Two hundred people: reasoning that travels without its author](https://lowob.com/research/two-hundred-people-reasoning-that-travels-without-its-author/)

Published 2026-10-14. At a few hundred people, founders make a small fraction of decisions, managers inherit precedents from people they never met, and turnover is constant. The decision record's job becomes delegation: formal decision classes, a precedent slot, standard handover packs and a first calibration, without sliding into compliance theatre.

## [Fifty people: when words start to mean different things](https://lowob.com/research/fifty-people-when-words-start-to-mean-different-things/)

Published 2026-10-12. At around fifty people, teams form and vocabularies drift, and AI tools amplify the confusion. The decision record's job becomes meaning: a short glossary with owners, written decision rights, a conflicts list, and one company-owned place where records live, which every new AI tool must write to.

## [Ten people: the first stranger](https://lowob.com/research/ten-people-the-first-stranger/)

Published 2026-10-09. Somewhere between the third and tenth hire, a company gains people who were not there when anything was decided. The decision record's job becomes answering 'why do we do it this way?' without a founder in the room. A topic wiki is the trap; a time-ordered ledger readable by strangers, with a few 'why we do it' pages and first definitions, is the defence.

## [Raise, Rally, Revenue: the whole series on one page](https://lowob.com/research/raise-rally-revenue/)

Published 2026-10-07. Fundraising, community and customers are one system, not three projects, and it runs in a fixed order: name the buyer, write one truth, collect evidence, raise against it, give the community a job, make first customers design partners, distribute, measure, then hand over. 2026 funding and buyer data make the order matter more: capital is concentrated, buyers fund from new budgets, and platforms send less traffic.

## [Two people: the founders' ledger](https://lowob.com/research/two-people-the-founders-ledger/)

Published 2026-10-07. At two people, the enterprise brain is a single append-only decision document and a 30-minute weekly review. Its job is to stop two honest founders remembering the same decision differently, a problem with good evidence behind it, and it is worth more than any tool at this stage.

## [The scale ladder](https://lowob.com/research/the-scale-ladder/)

Published 2026-10-06. There is no single right enterprise brain; the right one depends on the organisation's stage. Each size, from two people to ten thousand, has a different problem for the decision record to solve: false shared memory, the first stranger, meaning, delegation, governance and density. This hub sets out the whole ladder, what to build at each rung, the risk at each, and the five invariants that hold at every size.

## [Built to be kept without us](https://lowob.com/research/built-to-be-kept-without-us/)

Published 2026-10-02. The honest test of a judgment system, and of anyone who installs one, is whether it keeps working after they leave. That requires client ownership, full export, documented routines and a handover pack. Regulators in the EU and UK now treat switching barriers as a market problem, but no law makes a record readable without its builders. A record nobody maintains depreciates, so the handover should include a small maintenance rhythm.

## [Handovers are where reasoning pours out](https://lowob.com/research/handovers-are-where-reasoning-pours-out/)

Published 2026-10-01. Organisations leak reasons constantly, but at handovers the reasoning behind live decisions leaves all at once, on a known date. That makes the handover the cheapest and most obvious place to start a judgment record. A five-part handover pack, started four weeks before departure, captures what a standard document dump loses.

## [The Agency You Hired Spent $50K. What Did You Actually Get?](https://lowob.com/research/the-agency-spent-50k-and-i-have-nothing-to-point-at/)

Published 2026-10-01. When an agency has spent the budget and nothing connects to a customer, the money usually went out before measurement, ownership or an agreed result existed. Separate fees, media and production; get the accounts and data into the company's name; agree what counts as a result; then decide whether the current agency can improve. None of this makes the agency dishonest; it makes the setup wrong.

## [Below the volume floor](https://lowob.com/research/below-the-volume-floor/)

Published 2026-09-29. At around 150 material decisions a year, all different, no model will learn a company's judgment, and pooling across companies does not rescue it. What works is the company's own prior reasoning, recorded properly, plus public base rates, read and argued with by a person. Forecasting research supports starting from the reference class.

## [Reviewer minutes per useful decision](https://lowob.com/research/reviewer-minutes-per-useful-decision/)

Published 2026-09-28. The number that decides whether an AI judgment system pays for itself is human review time per decision that actually helped, not token cost. Productivity research predicts that metric will rise before it falls. Put the crossover date in writing at the start, and treat a miss as a decision to redesign, narrow or reprice.

## [The humans carrying context are the price signal](https://lowob.com/research/the-humans-carrying-context-are-the-price-signal/)

Published 2026-09-24. Enterprises are paying forward-deployed engineers to carry the context their software cannot hold, and that spending is the clearest market price for a missing organisational record. Spend data shows the context layer underfunded relative to models. The fix is not removing the people but making their context a client-owned deliverable.

## ["We shipped everything and the number went down"](https://lowob.com/research/we-shipped-everything-and-the-number-went-down/)

Published 2026-09-24. If the product is proven and the core number still fell, the problem has moved to distribution. Most shipped features are rarely used and most ideas do not move the metric, so more releases are not the fix. Stop building for sixty days, name one lead story you can prove, work one channel, usually partners who already have your buyer, and report the number with and without incentives.

## [Whoever holds the record holds the company](https://lowob.com/research/whoever-holds-the-record-holds-the-company/)

Published 2026-09-23. The layer that encodes how a business decides is becoming the deepest lock-in in enterprise software, and analysts now tell vendors to capture customer-specific knowledge rather than data. Models are rented and switched; the decision record is not. The enterprise should own that record, and the contract should say so before the first workflow moves in.

## [A reviewer who does not verify is not a control](https://lowob.com/research/a-reviewer-who-does-not-verify-is-not-a-control/)

Published 2026-09-21. Human-in-the-loop is a design pattern, not a defence. Courts, regulators and clients now look for evidence that the human actually checked, and the human factors research shows that instructions alone do not make people check. Design the review gate so that it produces verification evidence as a by-product.

## ["40,000 members and nobody does anything"](https://lowob.com/research/40-000-members-and-nobody-does-anything/)

Published 2026-09-18. A large, silent community was usually recruited for a payout and never given a job. Pick one job, recruit thirty people by name, ask them for judgment on a real decision, close the loop in public, and count who stays when incentives stop.

## [Regulators want the chain, not the model](https://lowob.com/research/regulators-want-the-chain-not-the-model/)

Published 2026-09-18. Financial supervisors in the US, UK and EU are not asking to inspect your model; they want you to reconstruct what it did, step by step, and who checked. This guide maps what each regime expects to be reconstructable and for how long, and sets out a field-by-field specification for an AI decision record. That record is also what a judgment system needs to learn, so build it once as the product's spine.

## [Where judgment arrives first](https://lowob.com/research/where-judgment-arrives-first/)

Published 2026-09-16. AI judgment layers will work first where decisions are frequent, similar and graded quickly, and where someone will later have to defend them. Research on expertise points the same way: judgment can be learned only in environments regular enough to learn from, with feedback. Map decision classes on volume and outcome lag before choosing where to build; elsewhere, judgment is a practice before it is a product.

## [The graveyard](https://lowob.com/research/the-graveyard/)

Published 2026-09-15. The most valuable thing an organisation knows is what it tried and abandoned, and why, and it is the first thing lost when people move. Research on organisational forgetting and on lessons-learned systems shows both the loss and why most archives go unread. A judgment system should make the graveyard first-class, distinguish what was disproven from what was merely under-tried, and surface the closest record when a new proposal is made.

## [Approval rate measures fatigue too](https://lowob.com/research/approval-rate-measures-fatigue-too/)

Published 2026-09-11. "Accepted without edit" rises when an AI system improves, but also when reviewers tire, trust fluent output, see only easy cases, or accept blander work. Clinical alert research and automation-bias studies show why. Report approval rate only beside an independently measured error rate and a seeded-error catch rate.

## ["The round has stalled"](https://lowob.com/research/the-round-has-stalled/)

Published 2026-09-11. A stalled round is either a process fault or an evidence gap, and the pass reasons tell you which. Read every pass, fix the gap or pause cleanly, then compress the remaining live conversations into a two-week window. In a 2026 market where capital is concentrating in fewer companies, a stall is common and usually diagnosable.

## [Dissent is the data you are throwing away](https://lowob.com/research/dissent-is-the-data-you-are-throwing-away/)

Published 2026-09-10. When a committee decides, the minority view is smoothed out of the record, and group research shows discussion tends to bury information only some members hold. Capture independent views before discussion in one attributed line with a probability, review them against outcomes, and protect dissenters.

## [Calibration is the honest learning signal](https://lowob.com/research/calibration-is-the-honest-learning-signal/)

Published 2026-09-08. A system cannot claim to learn by grading its own outputs. It can by comparing human predictions, made with a probability before the decision, against outcomes it did not produce. Rating agencies have published this kind of scorecard for decades, and forecasting research shows calibration can be trained. Enterprises can extend it to renewals, approvals and pricing for one number per decision.

## [The field that makes a record a judgment](https://lowob.com/research/the-field-that-makes-a-record-a-judgment/)

Published 2026-09-07. A decision record without a stated falsifier is a press release. The one field that turns it into judgment is "what would prove this wrong, by when": a measure, a threshold, a date and an observer. It turns a decision into a prediction that can be graded, and it reveals at the moment of decision whether the people agreeing actually agree.

## ["The story isn't landing"](https://lowob.com/research/the-story-isnt-landing/)

Published 2026-09-07. When a pitch story isn't landing, the deck is usually aimed at the wrong audience, built on a category word instead of a buyer, or hiding its evidence too late. Fix those three structural faults before touching anything else. Seed decks now get less than two minutes of reading on average, so the evidence has to come first.

## [Discord Is Not a Community Strategy. Neither Is Telegram.](https://lowob.com/research/discord-telegram-community-strategy/)

Published 2026-09-05. Opening a Discord or Telegram makes a Web3 project feel operational before the relationships and operating system exist. Start from the jobs members need done, build the smallest set of spaces that serves them, treat moderation and security messaging as product design, and move durable knowledge out of chat. Choose the platform after the behaviour.

## [The Modular GTM Team: Specialist Depth Without a Full-Service Agency](https://lowob.com/research/the-modular-gtm-team/)

Published 2026-09-04. AI and Web3 companies often need specialist depth for short periods without carrying every specialist on payroll. A modular GTM team keeps a small senior core accountable for the commercial problem and brings in focused support when the bottleneck changes. Large advertisers already work this way, keeping most work in-house and buying agencies for capacity and specialist skill. The model works only if one team stays accountable for the outcome.

## [Keep the sources; let the summary regenerate](https://lowob.com/research/keep-the-sources-let-the-summary-regenerate/)

Published 2026-09-03. A generated summary must never be the only surviving copy of a decision, because every summary is a lossy compression made by one model on one day. Research finds model summaries drop qualifiers and add unsupported content. Keep immutable source snapshots, treat each summary as a regenerable, versioned view over them, and handle deletion with tombstones.

## [The false premise is the expensive failure](https://lowob.com/research/the-false-premise-is-the-expensive-failure/)

Published 2026-09-02. AI systems have become good at saying 'I don't know' but remain bad at saying 'that's not right any more'. In the 2026 MemTrace benchmark, a widely used memory layer abstained correctly 99.3% of the time but resolved premises that contradicted its memory only 14.6% of the time. The fix is a premise check against the record, tested on your own superseded views.

## [How to Run a Marketing RFP Without Wasting a Quarter](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-run-a-marketing-rfp/)

Published 2026-09-01. Most marketing RFPs select for the best proposal writer, not the best partner, and they are expensive: an ANA and 4A's study put the cost of a typical US agency review at about $1 million across client and agencies. A good RFP describes the real situation and outcome, asks for approach and evidence rather than free work, and weights category experience and fee incentives over polish. Better still: a short brief, a few conversations and a paid first engagement.

## [A Distribution Plan for a Product the Platforms Restrict: One Fintech Company, Ninety Days.](https://lowob.com/research/restricted-category-distribution-worked-example/)

Published 2026-09-01. A composite consumer fintech with two rejected ad accounts and an unspent budget works through the method over ninety days: a band map built from the platforms' own policies, a one-week test of three open channels with written thresholds, one channel built properly, and the rest added in proportion. No channel ends above half of funded accounts, and nothing depended on getting past a review.

## [AI Is Making Execution Cheap. Judgment Is Becoming the Marketing Moat.](https://lowob.com/research/judgment-is-the-moat/)

Published 2026-08-31. AI has made marketing output fast and cheap, and most B2B teams now use it to create content under pressure to produce more. Volume is no longer a differentiator. The advantage moves to judgment: choosing the problem, checking the claims, keeping an accountable person on consequential decisions, and measuring what changed rather than what shipped.

## [Revenue models for long cycles](https://lowob.com/research/revenue-models-for-long-cycles/)

Published 2026-08-31. Pick an emerging tech revenue model by who carries the capital and the service tail, price pilots and production differently, and report only what would survive due diligence. Gross margin per unit including measured service cost decides whether any model works, and contracted cash flows decide whether the units can be financed with debt instead of equity.

## [Supersede, never overwrite](https://lowob.com/research/supersede-never-overwrite/)

Published 2026-08-31. A memory that edits itself in place cannot explain itself, because the change is the information. Judgment records should keep two dates, when a view was true and when it was held, and replace old views by linked supersession rather than editing them. Databases, architecture decision records and at least one agent-memory design already work this way.

## [Retrieval is not the bottleneck](https://lowob.com/research/retrieval-is-not-the-bottleneck/)

Published 2026-08-28. Independent benchmarks find that AI memory systems usually retrieve the right evidence and then fail to use it, especially when facts have changed. Better search will not fix that. Giving every piece of evidence a standing, with status, validity dates, provenance and supersession links, and answering change questions with a timeline, will.

## [From Hype to Revenue: Web3's Next Competitive Advantage Is Operating Discipline](https://lowob.com/research/from-hype-to-revenue/)

Published 2026-08-27. Web3 has never struggled to generate attention; converting it into a durable business is the hard part. The evidence on incentive-led launches shows attention fading within weeks, and US regulators are now asking token projects for principles-based disclosure of token economics and, for larger raises, GAAP financial statements. The advantage goes to teams that start from a commercial objective, test it with the smallest credible campaign and keep only what persists.

## [What Thought Leadership Actually Is](https://lowob.com/research/what-thought-leadership-actually-is/)

Published 2026-08-27. Thought leadership is a defensible position, supported by evidence the audience could not assemble, with a consequence for the reader, sustained over time. Edelman and LinkedIn's research finds buyers reward evidence and challenge, and drop vendors whose thinking is weak. Most of what carries the name is agreeable content measured by impressions. The real thing comes from a founder's actual thinking, on a cadence the founder can sustain.

## [The reason nobody types](https://lowob.com/research/the-reason-nobody-types/)

Published 2026-08-26. The operative reason for many decisions is political, personal, embarrassing or legally sensitive, so a system that records only the sayable reason produces clean, coherent and quietly false records. Research on organisational silence, psychological safety and premortems explains why, and AI-drafted rationales make it worse. No design fully fixes this, but a completeness flag, scoped visibility, a cynic's question and outcome write-back make it much better.

## [Ask for the gap, not the summary](https://lowob.com/research/ask-for-the-gap-not-the-summary/)

Published 2026-08-25. A good judgment system does not ask people to summarise everything. It compares each live decision record against a template of what that decision class needs, finds the most important missing item, and asks one specific question of the person most likely to know. Alert-fatigue and context research explain why one question beats five.

## [Integrators, OEMs and channel partners](https://lowob.com/research/integrators-oems-and-channel-partners/)

Published 2026-08-25. In emerging tech the buyer already trusts someone else's hands, so the job is to make integrators and partners want to carry you, one partner at a time. Canalys estimated 70% of technology spending in 2025 would go through partners. Do the first deployments direct, productise the playbook, and measure only partner-sourced pipeline that reaches paid pilot.

## [Web3 Does Not Have One Customer. That Is Why Most Launch Plans Break.](https://lowob.com/research/web3-multi-audience-launch-plan/)

Published 2026-08-25. A protocol may need users, developers, capital providers, distribution partners, institutions and governance participants before it works, and each is waiting for evidence from another. Map the groups, launch in the order the dependencies require, keep one product truth explained differently for each, and measure participation rather than attention. In the EU and US, consistency across audiences is now also a regulatory expectation.

## [Intent, not a destination](https://lowob.com/research/intent-not-a-destination/)

Published 2026-08-21. Every interaction a judgment system records should serve an explicit outcome, but naming the conclusion in advance bends the reasoning to reach it. Research on sycophancy and unfaithful explanations shows models follow the framing they are given and justify it fluently. The craft is keeping the purpose fixed and the answer open: name the decision, ask in a fixed schema, and make advocacy a separate, paired step.

## [What Makes a Case Study Believable](https://lowob.com/research/what-makes-a-case-study-believable/)

Published 2026-08-21. A case study is evidence, not advertising. A believable one keeps the specific situation, the real sequence including setbacks, dated numbers with a baseline and the customer's own voice, even when the name has to go. Research on reviews and two-sided messages suggests some acknowledged weakness raises credibility, and US rules treat testimonials as claims that need substantiation.

## [Clipping Is Not a Fad. It Is Paid Distribution With a Human Face.](https://lowob.com/research/clipping-paid-distribution/)

Published 2026-08-20. A clipping programme pays many small accounts, usually $1 to $5 per thousand views, to cut long-form content into short clips and post them. Treated as paid media, it has a price, a yield and a set of controls: verified views, written edit rules, disclosure on every clip and a cost per outcome compared with every other channel.

## [The trade must clear on the spot](https://lowob.com/research/the-trade-must-clear-on-the-spot/)

Published 2026-08-20. People share what they know when they get something back in the same moment. A promise of future collective value is a public-goods problem, and two decades of research on knowledge sharing show it gets under-supplied. Knowledge capture should give a private, immediate, visible return: precedent, a warning, work done for them, or credit when their record is reused.

## [First customers in a market that doesn't exist yet](https://lowob.com/research/first-customers-in-a-market-that-doesnt-exist-yet/)

Published 2026-08-19. In a market that does not exist yet, first customers are chosen as design partners and references at once, bought through institutional procurement, reached through practitioner networks and standards bodies, and measured by risk retired rather than pipeline value. This playbook adds the facts that shape those pilots: UK procurement thresholds, how selective regulator sandboxes are, and where AI standards are being written.

## [A loop with good context](https://lowob.com/research/a-loop-with-good-context/)

Published 2026-08-18. An agent is a loop, so the engineering that matters is what the loop knows when it asks. Research on long inputs shows that more context makes models less reliable, so teams must choose what enters. The most valuable context almost nobody supplies is prior judgment on comparable cases, delivered through a precedent slot filled before each task runs and tested blind.

## [Community Management vs Social Media Management](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-social-media-management/)

Published 2026-08-18. Social media management is editorial: the company's voice on its own accounts. Community management is hosting: members' voices in spaces the company runs. The two jobs have different daily work, measures and temperaments, and combining them by default sets one of them up to be neglected. This guide sets out what each requires and how to staff them at different sizes.

## [The first two-fifths](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-two-fifths/)

Published 2026-08-17. What has shipped as an "enterprise brain" is the context layer: knowledge and governance, the easy two-fifths of the idea, with meaning built in a few places. Memory is arriving as a feature but does not yet track change, and judgment is skipped, because nothing in the stack writes an outcome back to a decision.

## [KOL Campaigns Need More Than Impression Screenshots](https://lowob.com/research/web3-kol-campaign-measurement/)

Published 2026-08-16. Impression screenshots show that content was delivered, not that anyone understood or used the product. Define the behaviour you are buying, instrument the path from click to wallet action before paying, judge creators on distribution, activation, durability and economics, and make the second payment conditional on evidence. Disclosure is part of the brief: US, UK and EU rules all treat a paid crypto post as advertising.

## [Raising for long cycles](https://lowob.com/research/raising-for-long-cycles/)

Published 2026-08-12. Long-cycle companies raise against milestones, not time. Build a capital stack that mixes dilutive, non-dilutive, strategic and project money, each matched to the risk it can carry, and show investors one retired risk per round. With a median two years between seed and Series A, runway has to cover the full sales cycle plus the next raise.

## [Event, Newsletter, and Podcast Sponsorships Explained](https://lowob.com/research/sponsorships-events-newsletters-podcasts/)

Published 2026-08-12. Sponsorships buy the trust of an audience someone else assembled. Pay for access and explanation rather than visibility, check the property's real numbers, including how downloads and opens are counted, track with codes and links, and define the observable outcome before signing.

## [The Channels Nobody Can Take Away From You Are the Ones You Keep Neglecting.](https://lowob.com/research/owned-channels-email-content/)

Published 2026-08-10. Owned channels are the ones where a company holds the relationship directly: email, content on its own site, the search presence that content earns, and the product's own messages. They are slow and thinly bid, which is why they compound. With search clicks falling and platform rules shifting, build email first, give every piece of content a job, and route every rented channel to an address the company keeps.

## [Founder, Brand and Community Accounts Need Different Jobs](https://lowob.com/research/founder-brand-community-social-strategy/)

Published 2026-08-07. When a founder, company and community account all repeat the same announcement, people have fewer reasons to follow each one. Give the founder judgment, the company clarity and proof, and the community participation. Cascade one fact through three voices, decide who speaks in a crisis before it happens, and run the system from an operating matrix.

## [How to Read a Creator Media Kit](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-creator-media-kit/)

Published 2026-08-07. A creator media kit is a sales document prepared by the seller. Read past the follower count to median engagement, real demographics and repeat sponsors, ask for the numbers it leaves out, check for paid relationships and fake metrics, and test on cost-per-outcome terms before buying a package.

## [Selling what nobody has a budget line for](https://lowob.com/research/selling-what-nobody-has-a-budget-line-for/)

Published 2026-08-06. When no budget line exists, sell against the cost of what the buyer does today, through a category they already recognise, to the person who owns the pain. The real competitor is the status quo: research on 2.5 million sales calls found 40% to 60% of lost deals end in no decision. The category story is for investors; customers buy a specific problem solved this quarter.

## [What Is UGC, and Why Brands Now Pay for It](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ugc/)

Published 2026-08-03. UGC now means two things: genuine customer content, credible because it was not commissioned, and paid creator content styled to look organic, which performs in paid social. Use both, keep them distinct, and disclose and review the paid kind as the advertising it is, including the FTC's rules on actual consumers, typical results and fake reviews.

## [In Emerging Tech, the Only Strategy Question Is Which Bets You Can Take Back.](https://lowob.com/research/emerging-tech-reversible-bets/)

Published 2026-08-02. Companies in emerging categories are told to move fast and to be careful. Both are true, and the way to hold them together is a sorting rule: make reversible decisions quickly, cheaply and in parallel, and irreversible ones slowly, one at a time, after the reversible ones have produced evidence. This playbook applies the rule to AI and Web3, with the regulatory and market evidence that shows which decisions cannot be taken back.

## [From reach to recurring](https://lowob.com/research/from-reach-to-recurring/)

Published 2026-07-30. Reach is rented and recurring is owned. Google search traffic to publishers fell by a third in a year, and AI summaries cut clicks further. Media businesses should move to products people pay for repeatedly, measured by paid conversion, churn, revenue per subscriber, sponsor renewal and the share of revenue not dependent on platforms.

## [Your Customers Already Wrote Your Messaging. Claude Can Help You Find It.](https://lowob.com/research/claude-voice-of-customer-research/)

Published 2026-07-29. The strongest messaging is recovered from the market, not invented in a workshop, and the evidence sits scattered across calls, tickets, reviews and lost-deal notes. Claude can read that material at scale if the method is disciplined: structured extraction with quoted excerpts first, clustering by buying situation, a disagreement report against internal copy, and a monthly refresh. Research on AI coding shows why quotes matter: models match humans on explicit themes and fall short on interpretive ones.

## [What Is App Store Optimization? Fintech and Crypto Apps](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-app-store-optimization/)

Published 2026-07-29. App store optimization is improving how an app ranks in store search, converts from listing to install, and passes store review. Apple says nearly 65% of App Store downloads happen directly after a search, and both stores now offer native listing tests and keyword-targeted pages. For fintech and crypto apps that cannot buy installs freely, the store is open-band distribution every other channel depends on, so the listing is the channel.

## [What Is Marketing Mix Modeling? A Small-Company Guide](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-marketing-mix-modeling/)

Published 2026-07-24. Marketing mix modeling estimates each channel's total contribution to an outcome from aggregate weekly data, without tracking individuals. Google's Meridian and Meta's Robyn have made the method free, but both are clear that it needs history, variation and calibration. Combined with attribution and incrementality tests, it gives the most honest picture a company can assemble.

## [Your first ten sponsors are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-sponsors-are-design-partners/)

Published 2026-07-24. Sponsorship, data and research are B2B sales. Treat the first ten sponsors as design partners: agree a named audience segment, a success test and a two-way reporting format before any money moves, price the first campaign for evidence, and measure renewal from the first conversation.

## [Creator Partnerships Outside Crypto Make the Same Mistakes With Fewer Excuses.](https://lowob.com/research/creator-partnerships-fintech-ai/)

Published 2026-07-22. Web3 paid publicly to learn what creator partnerships do and do not do. Fintech and AI companies moving budget into the channel can read those lessons, and regulators have since made several of them law: the FTC's 2024 rule bans buying fake followers and views, and the FCA holds firms responsible for what their influencers promote. Run creators as a programme with terms, briefs, tracking, disclosure and pay per outcome.

## [What Is Ad Fraud? Bots, MFA Sites, and Controls](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ad-fraud/)

Published 2026-07-20. Ad fraud is any scheme that generates fake advertising activity so someone is paid for attention that never happened, and it hides inside good-looking reports. Estimates range from under 1% invalid traffic in TAG Certified channels to 22% of all online spend. Buy through inclusion lists with pre-bid verification, validate outcomes in your own systems and use partners not paid more when volume rises.

## [Airdrops Can Buy Attention. They Cannot Buy Belief.](https://lowob.com/research/airdrops-points-community-incentives/)

Published 2026-07-19. Airdrops, points, ambassador programmes and referral rewards are mechanism-design choices that redefine what participation means. The on-chain evidence shows most airdrops lose recipients and value quickly: Keyrock found most of 62 airdrops fell within 15 days, and academic work found up to 66% of claimed tokens went straight to exchanges. Reward contribution quality and persistence, count incentives as acquisition cost, and model what remains when the reward stops.

## [Membership is the job](https://lowob.com/research/membership-is-the-job/)

Published 2026-07-17. A media audience is a list until it becomes a membership: people who pay, show up, contribute and refer. With only 17% paying for online news across 20 markets in 2026, membership has to offer more than access. Build it on sourcing, peer amplification and peer value, keep it on channels you control, and measure it monthly like a business line.

## [Brand Safety vs Brand Suitability: What They Cost You](https://lowob.com/research/brand-safety-and-suitability/)

Published 2026-07-15. Brand safety keeps ads away from harmful content; brand suitability keeps them near content that fits the brand. Both are enforced by blunt tools that over-block by default: an IAS and Reuters analysis found a typical keyword blocklist would flag 54% of brand-suitable news URLs. GARM, the industry's shared framework, was discontinued in 2024, so each buyer now has to set its own standard.

## [In Fintech, Trust Is the Product and the Channel Is Whoever Already Has It.](https://lowob.com/research/fintech-gtm-trust-distribution/)

Published 2026-07-14. A fintech can beat an incumbent on price and experience and still struggle to acquire customers, because people are being asked to trust an unfamiliar company with their money. Ad platforms now verify financial advertisers before they run, and regulators hold firms responsible for what partners and influencers say. The channels that work are the people and platforms customers already trust, supplied with approved facts and measured on funded, retained use.

## [What investors fund in media now](https://lowob.com/research/what-investors-fund-in-media-now/)

Published 2026-07-13. Investors fund media businesses with owned audiences that pay, proprietary products those audiences need, and revenue that does not depend on a platform. Reach is the raw material, not the asset. With search traffic to publishers down a third and only 17% of people paying for online news, the evidence that counts is repeat behaviour: paid conversion, renewal, sponsor renewal and signed licensing.

## [Ad Network vs Ad Exchange vs DSP: The Middlemen](https://lowob.com/research/ad-network-vs-exchange-vs-dsp/)

Published 2026-07-09. Ad networks bundle and resell publisher inventory with little visibility, ad exchanges run real-time auctions, and DSPs are the software buyers use to bid. The DSP is where control lives. Audits by ISBA, PwC and the ANA show how much of a dollar each layer absorbs, and IAB Tech Lab standards show how to check who is selling.

## [Founder-Led GTM Is Not a Vibe. It Is a Job With an Expiration Date.](https://lowob.com/research/founder-led-gtm-expiration-date/)

Published 2026-07-08. Founder-led go-to-market is a phase, not an identity. Its purpose is to discover and encode a commercial motion that other people can operate. This playbook sets out what the founder should keep and hand off, a dependency test, a debrief that captures the founder's invisible decisions, and three stages from explorer to executive sponsor.

## [An audience is not a business](https://lowob.com/research/an-audience-is-not-a-business/)

Published 2026-07-06. An audience is an asset, not a business. A media business starts when you can say who the audience is, what it does, who pays for access to it and which part you own. With platforms now the main route to news and only 17% paying for online news in 2026, the owned audience and a claims register for every number are what buyers and investors check.

## [Native Advertising and Sponsored Content Explained](https://lowob.com/research/native-advertising-and-sponsored-content/)

Published 2026-07-06. Native advertising is paid placement that matches the form of the content around it; sponsored content is the subset where the advertiser supplies or commissions an actual piece. Both suit products that need explaining, but disclosure is not optional: the FTC, the EU's Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and the UK's ASA all require paid content to be clearly identifiable, and the advertiser is responsible alongside the publisher.

## [Attribution vs Incrementality: What Did Your Marketing Actually Cause?](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/)

Published 2026-07-04. Every attribution model is a story about who deserves credit; none measures what would have happened without the spend. Field experiments at Facebook and eBay show how far the stories can drift from the truth. This piece sets out the holdout designs a smaller company can run, how to read the result, and a three-layer measurement stack.

## [Claude Is Not Your Intern. Build a Repeatable GTM Workflow](https://lowob.com/research/claude-gtm-operating-system/)

Published 2026-07-01. Most teams use Claude like an intern with amnesia: a blank chat, a vague request, a fresh start tomorrow. Claude's Projects, Skills and connectors, as documented in November 2026, let a team hold commercial context, run named workflows and set approval rules for actions. The advantage is not access to the model but the context, procedures and learning loop a company builds around it.

## [From funded account to lifetime value](https://lowob.com/research/from-funded-account-to-lifetime-value/)

Published 2026-06-30. Revenue in fintech is a chain from acquisition to lifetime value. The two leaks that break it are accounts that never fund and accounts that fund once and go dormant. Measure the chain per channel, not blended, put fraud losses and compliance cost in the same table as revenue, and report active funded accounts as the growth number.

## [What Is Connected TV Advertising? Should You Buy It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-connected-tv-advertising/)

Published 2026-06-30. Connected TV is television watched through an internet connection, with advertising bought and measured like digital media. The IAB forecast US CTV spend growing 13.8% in 2026, and CTV was about 40% of programmatic spend in the ANA's Q4 2025 benchmark. It is best entered programmatically, measured by lift rather than clicks, and worth buying once a company has a working acquisition motion, a measurable brand constraint and confirmation its category is permitted.

## [What Is Retargeting, and Why It Overclaims Credit](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retargeting/)

Published 2026-06-25. Retargeting shows ads to people who already know the company, which makes it cheap and makes its attributed results unreliable. Field experiments find real but modest lift: one retailer's retargeting raised purchases by about 11%. Exclude people who converted, cap frequency, shorten windows, test with a holdout, and remember that email is retargeting you own.

## [One Channel Is Carrying You, and It Isn't Yours.](https://lowob.com/research/single-channel-dependency/)

Published 2026-06-24. The most dangerous distribution position is being visible on one channel someone else controls. Platform rules, ranking systems and click behaviour all shifted on dated announcements in 2024 to 2026. Price the dependency with three numbers, build a second channel with a different failure mode while the first still pays for it, and keep no channel above half of outcomes for more than two quarters.

## [The people who vouch for you](https://lowob.com/research/the-people-who-vouch-for-you/)

Published 2026-06-24. In fintech, your community is the practitioners who advise your segment and the customers willing to be named. Build a vouching system, not a chat room: give it three jobs (referrals, feedback, public trust signals), pay referrers openly where the rules allow it, and measure referred funded accounts and their retention. A bank study found referred customers stayed longer and were worth at least 16% more.

## [One Founder Interview Should Produce a Month of Content. Here Is the System.](https://lowob.com/research/founder-interview-content-engine/)

Published 2026-06-20. Founder content fails when the founder is asked to become a full-time creator or when marketing imitates a voice it cannot access. Treat the founder's time as a source session instead: one focused interview on one thesis, AI-assisted extraction, an asset tree where each piece has a different job, a voice sheet, and an approval ladder that keeps the founder off the critical path.

## [What SEO Is Now: How Search Ranking Works Today](https://lowob.com/research/what-seo-is-now/)

Published 2026-06-19. Modern SEO rewards pages that answer the query better than the alternatives, are technically sound and are trusted by other sites; it punishes volume and tricks. AI summaries now cut clicks on many informational queries by half or more, and AI assistants are a parallel channel that rewards the same things. Payback is slower than most plans assume, but every company should do the minimum.

## [Distribute through whoever already holds the customer](https://lowob.com/research/distribute-through-whoever-already-holds-the-customer/)

Published 2026-06-17. Fintech cannot buy its way to customers. Trust moves through partners who hold the relationship, practitioners who explain money, comparison and affiliate publishers, and owned channels. Paid goes last and small, because it is a reviewed category with low conversion rates, and the measures that matter are cost per funded account and retention, not sign-ups.

## [Email Deliverability Explained: SPF, DKIM, DMARC](https://lowob.com/research/email-deliverability-explained/)

Published 2026-06-16. Deliverability rests on three layers: authentication, reputation, and content and behaviour. Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook now require SPF, DKIM, DMARC, one-click unsubscribe and spam rates below 0.3% from bulk senders, and enforce it by rejecting mail. Set up the records, warm the domain, send only to people who asked, clean the list and watch the reports.

## [AI Companies Have a Distribution Problem Disguised as a Model Problem.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-companies-distribution-problem/)

Published 2026-06-15. Enterprise AI spend is large and growing, yet many AI products with strong demos still struggle to find paying customers. Buyers say most models are now good enough, procurement looks like ordinary software buying, and Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027 for cost and unclear value. This piece separates product problems from distribution and adoption problems and sets out how to diagnose which one a company has.

## [Forget 10,000 Followers. Find Your First 100 People Who Actually Care.](https://lowob.com/research/first-100-community-members/)

Published 2026-06-12. The first meaningful community milestone is 100 people who understand why the project matters and repeatedly choose to participate. This piece covers running that first group: defining caring as behaviour, a narrow member thesis, one recurring ritual, consequential roles, a weekly member-health review and growth through density.

## [How Marketing Teams Actually Use AI Tools](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-teams-use-ai/)

Published 2026-06-11. AI tools in marketing have settled into research, drafting, extraction, analysis and quality control, ideally working from shared context and named workflows with a human review rule. Surveys show near-universal use but gains mostly in speed, not quality, and few teams with rules on when not to use AI. The tools do not supply judgment, verified claims or contact with the market.

## [Raising in a regulated category](https://lowob.com/research/raising-in-a-regulated-category/)

Published 2026-06-11. Fintech investors underwrite trust and durability, not growth alone. Show the licence as an asset with a dated path, build unit economics per funded account, put compliance cost and losses in the model, and have a plan for when a partner bank leaves. The 2024 Synapse failure and a wave of 2026 US charter approvals have made the partner bank question the first one experienced investors ask.

## [Performance Marketing Is Not a Channel. It Is a Way of Paying.](https://lowob.com/research/performance-marketing-way-of-paying/)

Published 2026-06-06. Performance marketing means paying when something happens rather than when something is shown. It works only when the outcome is observable in the company's own tracking, attributable with enough confidence to pay against, and worth the payment. This piece sets out the three conditions, the evidence on where last-click payment goes wrong, four weekly numbers and the honest limits.

## [What Is Conversion Rate Optimization, and When to Do It](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-conversion-rate-optimization/)

Published 2026-06-05. Conversion rate optimization increases the share of visitors who sign up, apply, fund, buy or book, through diagnosis, hypothesis, testing and measurement. Baymard's checkout research shows how much loss comes from fixable friction. It needs enough traffic to test, the conversion the business actually runs on, and the right visitors; if the visitors were never going to buy, the problem is upstream.

## [Trust is the product](https://lowob.com/research/trust-is-the-product/)

Published 2026-06-04. In fintech, trust is the product and the feature list is secondary. Trust is borrowed from institutions the buyer already trusts, proved in the order buyers check, and every claim about money is compliance copy that should come from a claims register. Recent rules make the custodian question sharper: the FDIC treats a non-bank's failure to say it is not a bank as a material omission, and UK payment and e-money funds sit outside the FSCS.

## [Landing Pages and Ad Review: Why Yours Gets Rejected](https://lowob.com/research/landing-pages-and-ad-review/)

Published 2026-06-02. A landing page does one job for one source and is reviewed by the ad platform before the visitor sees it. Google's destination, misrepresentation and financial services rules spell out most of what reviewers check. To pass and convert, match the ad, disclose the business, make compliant claims, answer the visitor's doubts, and never show reviewers and users different pages.

## [You Are Buying Media and You Do Not Trust the Numbers. You Are Right Not To.](https://lowob.com/research/programmatic-media-numbers-you-can-trust/)

Published 2026-06-02. Programmatic reports are built to be legible, not true. The ANA found only 36 cents of each dollar entering a buying platform reached a consumer, so the reported CPM understates the price of impressions that could have mattered. This playbook sets out how to calculate a real CPM, why the rejection rate is the number to watch, and six questions to ask before the next invoice.

## [Protocol revenue: what the protocol keeps and what to report](https://lowob.com/research/protocol-revenue-fees-real-yield-and-what-to-report/)

Published 2026-05-29. Report what the protocol keeps, with and without incentives, where it came from and what it cost to get, on one page, monthly, in the same format. TVL is a balance, not revenue; protocol revenue is the fee income retained after suppliers are paid. The SEC's 2026 offering proposal points the same way, asking for token economics and, for larger raises, GAAP financial statements.

## [Cold Outreach Works Better With a Real Reason to Talk](https://lowob.com/research/signal-based-outbound/)

Published 2026-05-28. Personalisation theatre, a line about the prospect's podcast on top of a generic pitch, is not a reason to talk. Signal-based outbound starts from an observable change in the prospect's business, scores it for recency, relevance, magnitude, access and proof, and writes from a hypothesis. With about 95% of buyers out of market at any time, the discipline is as much about who not to contact as who to contact.

## [What Is Account-Based Marketing? A Small-Team Version](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-account-based-marketing/)

Published 2026-05-27. Account-based marketing concentrates marketing and sales effort on a named list of accounts worth winning. It fits complex, high-value sales to identifiable buyers, where purchases involve around 13 people. A small team can run it with a short list, research, one owner per account and measures that track account movement rather than email volume.

## [Build an Affiliate Program Without Paying for Coupon Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/)

Published 2026-05-25. An affiliate program is a set of terms under which other people are paid to bring you customers. Badly designed terms pay coupon sites and browser extensions for sales that would have happened anyway. Design the terms before choosing a network, recruit the first partners by hand, and judge the program on approved outcomes, partner mix and concentration.

## [Issuers, integrations and curators](https://lowob.com/research/issuers-integrations-and-curators/)
