Published 2026-05-22. When paid channels are closed, crypto distribution comes from people who already want you to succeed: issuers, integrations, curators and ecosystems. Google bans ads for DeFi protocols everywhere and the UK bans refer-a-friend bonuses for crypto, so work that list before spending on reach, and keep every piece of copy free of APYs and yield promises.

## [Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth](https://lowob.com/research/product-led-vs-sales-led-vs-partner-led/)

Published 2026-05-22. Product-led, sales-led and partner-led growth are different organizations, not just different tactics. Choose the primary motion from the product and the buyer, build the organization for it, and add the others in support. Restricted categories tilt the choice towards partners and relationships.

## [Community that survives the airdrop](https://lowob.com/research/community-that-survives-the-airdrop/)

Published 2026-05-18. Incentives buy activity, not community. On-chain studies of major airdrops show most recipients sell quickly and few stay active. Plan the airdrop as an acquisition cost, allocate for repeated use, give holders a real job and measure who keeps using the product after the payments stop.

## [Audience vs Community: What Actually Makes the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-audience/)

Published 2026-05-18. A large follower count or Discord server is not automatically a community. The difference is whether people help, learn from and create value for one another. This piece separates audiences, users, network participants and communities, sets out the peer-value test, and lists the measures that show which one a company actually has.

## [What Is a Marketing Funnel, and When Does It Help?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-marketing-funnel/)

Published 2026-05-18. The marketing funnel is a useful model of stages that need different things and a poor model of how individuals actually buy. Google and Gartner research both find buyers loop rather than descend. Find the stage that limits revenue now, concentrate there, and treat "full-funnel" as a warning sign rather than a plan.

## [How to Write an Ideal Customer Profile Sales Will Use](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-write-an-icp/)

Published 2026-05-13. An ideal customer profile is a narrow, evidence-based description of the customer a company should pursue first: most likely to buy, succeed and stay. It includes firmographics, situational triggers, the buying committee, disqualifiers and evidence. If every prospect qualifies, it is not an ICP.

## [A $10,000 Test That Closes a Question Beats a $10,000 Bet That Leaves It Open.](https://lowob.com/research/tests-that-close-questions/)

Published 2026-05-13. Most growth tests are small versions of what the company already wanted to do, and they end in "promising". A test closes a question when the threshold and the decision on each side are written before any money is spent. Measure two or three channels cheaply and in parallel, read the results against the thresholds, then commit budget to one channel at a time.

## [Token or no token](https://lowob.com/research/token-or-no-token/)

Published 2026-05-12. A token should reduce coordination cost or create ownership; if it does neither, do not issue one. If you do, the money you raise decides your go-to-market, and float, release schedules, stablecoin runway and liquidity depth matter more than headline FDV. The 2026 US and EU position makes what you promise in public part of the legal analysis, so legal belongs inside GTM.

## [Percent of Spend Is a Conflict of Interest With a Logo on It.](https://lowob.com/research/percent-of-spend-media-fees/)

Published 2026-05-09. Media agencies paid a percentage of spend earn more when clients spend more, not when the spending works. ANA research has documented rebates, principal-based markups and commissions that persist for media long after other services moved to fees. lowob runs media on three rules: a flat fee per account, no fronted spend, and fixed fees against written scope.

## [Positioning vs Messaging vs Branding: Which Is Broken?](https://lowob.com/research/positioning-vs-messaging-vs-branding/)

Published 2026-05-07. Positioning is the decision about where the company sits, messaging is the words that carry it, and branding is how the company is recognized. Diagnose and fix them in that order, because a brand refresh cannot fix a positioning problem. A five-person sentence test shows which layer is broken.

## [The user story before the token story](https://lowob.com/research/the-user-story-before-the-token-story/)

Published 2026-05-05. Write what the protocol does for a user in one sentence with no token in it; if you cannot, you have an instrument, not a product. Then give each audience one belief and one piece of evidence, and keep a claims register with no yield numbers, no 'safe' and every audit named and dated. MiCA and the SEC's 2026 interpretation both make public claims part of the legal record.

## [What Is a Distribution Diagnostic? One Week, Explained](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-distribution-diagnostic/)

Published 2026-05-04. A distribution diagnostic is a short, paid, scoped piece of work that answers which channels can carry a product to its buyer, what each costs, and where the next serious money should go. It has a fixed duration, price and written output, runs small real tests, and carries no obligation to continue. A week can show whether a channel is open and converts at all; it cannot replace the four to six weeks platforms recommend for a controlled experiment.

## [AI Did Not Fix Your Marketing. It Made Your Mediocrity Cheaper.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-made-average-marketing-cheaper/)

Published 2026-05-03. When every company has the same models, production speed stops being an advantage and the scarce inputs become judgment, access, evidence and a point of view. Research shows AI help makes individual work better but collective work more alike, and marketers credit AI with speed far more than quality. The fix is a proprietary-input test before publishing and a point-of-view ledger that feeds the calendar.

## [Thin Bidding: The Cheapest Attention Is Wherever Nobody Else Is Buying.](https://lowob.com/research/thin-bidding/)

Published 2026-04-30. The first cause of what a click costs is crowding: how many companies bid for the same person at the same moment. Alphabet, Amazon and Meta take about 56% of global ad spend, and the crowd follows them. Bidding thins where channels are unglamorous, inconvenient or closed to a category, and thin channels reward buyers who measure before they commit.

## [Brand vs Performance Marketing: Different Time Horizons](https://lowob.com/research/brand-vs-performance-marketing/)

Published 2026-04-29. Brand and performance marketing are not rivals; they work on different clocks. Performance buys measurable outcomes now, while brand makes future outcomes more likely and cheaper. The IPA evidence puts the long-run optimum near 60:40 brand to activation for consumer brands and 46:54 in B2B. Most small companies should fund performance first, then shift a growing share toward brand, measuring each on its own timescale.

## [Seats, usage or outcomes](https://lowob.com/research/seats-usage-or-outcomes/)

Published 2026-04-29. There are three ways to charge for an AI product, seats, usage and outcomes, and most companies now combine them. This guide sets out the fit test, real published price points from Microsoft, Salesforce, Intercom and Zendesk, a worked cost-per-task and gross-margin example, the contract terms that protect both sides and the eight monthly numbers that show whether the business works.

## [Your Startup Needs a GTM Strategy, Not Just a List of Tactics](https://lowob.com/research/gtm-strategy-vs-tactics/)

Published 2026-04-25. A list of channels and campaigns is not a go-to-market strategy. A strategy makes four connected decisions (market, message, motion and measurement) and every tactic then has a specific job inside them. This playbook sets out the decisions, a coherence test and seven questions to answer before approving another campaign.

## [How to Read a Media Plan Before You Approve It](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-media-plan/)

Published 2026-04-23. A media plan says where a marketing budget will be spent, over what period, in what proportions, and what each part should produce. Before approving one, read the objective, the expected outcomes and the cost basis, check the programmatic supply path, and ask what the plan assumes, what happens when a channel fails, and who owns the data afterwards.

## [Raising for an AI company](https://lowob.com/research/raising-for-an-ai-company/)

Published 2026-04-22. AI took 82.7% of US venture deal value through September 2026, but most of it went to model companies and very large rounds. Application companies are priced like software companies, on retention, margin and replaceability, with two extra costs: inference and platform risk. Raise on gross margin net of inference, falling cost per task and retained production usage, and put the model in the appendix.

## [Meta Said No. That Is Not the End of Your Distribution Plan.](https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-ad-platforms-restrict-you/)

Published 2026-04-21. A rejected ad account is a decision about your category, made by a reviewer who never sees the product. Sort every channel into open, restricted and closed bands for each geography, build first where the answer is already yes, and file restricted-band paperwork with nothing forecast against it. Google, Meta and TikTok all tightened or re-scoped financial and crypto rules in 2025 and 2026, so the map needs a date on it.

## [How Marketing Services Are Priced: Five Fee Models](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-services-are-priced/)

Published 2026-04-20. Marketing services are priced five ways: retainer, project fee, hourly or daily, percent of spend, and performance. Each rewards the provider for something different. Large advertisers are moving away from paying for time, and AI is speeding the shift, but most still lack visibility into what agencies earn. Find what makes the fee go up and you have found the advice you will get.

## [Developers, marketplaces and the answer engines](https://lowob.com/research/developers-marketplaces-and-the-answer-engines/)

Published 2026-04-16. AI distribution runs through the platforms you plug into, the assistants buyers ask, and the people who build on you. This piece sets out how to pick one lead motion, what cloud marketplaces and model-provider directories actually require and charge, how to show up correctly when buyers ask an assistant, and why paid acquisition comes last.

## [What Is a Restricted Category in Advertising?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-restricted-category/)

Published 2026-04-14. Ad platforms sort products into prohibited, restricted and open groups, using a process built to refuse a legitimate business rather than approve a harmful one. Google, Meta, TikTok and Apple each publish the conditions, and they change them often. A restricted classification is a map of where to build distribution, not a review to argue with or evade.

## [The pilot that survives security review](https://lowob.com/research/the-pilot-that-survives-security-review/)

Published 2026-04-09. AI pilots die from security review, missing owners, demo-grade accuracy and pricing confusion, rarely from the product. Gartner expected at least 30% of generative AI projects to be abandoned after proof of concept. This playbook sets out the pilot design that passes: one narrow use case, real data in week one, a written success test, a security pack mapped to the questionnaires buyers actually send (SIG, CAIQ and SOC 2), a named owner and a paid fee.

## [What Go-to-Market Means: A Plain Guide for Founders](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-gtm-for-founders/)

Published 2026-04-09. Go-to-market is the plan for how a company finds customers, convinces them to buy, and does so at a cost that leaves a business. It is four decisions that must agree: who exactly, what they must believe, how trust moves, and what evidence proves it is working. A company has a GTM when it can write one sentence for each and the four sentences agree.

## [How Marketing Tracking Works: Pixels to Server-Side](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-tracking-works/)

Published 2026-04-03. Pixels see less every year and platforms fill the gaps with modelled estimates. Safari blocks third-party cookies by default, Apple requires permission to track across apps, and Chrome kept third-party cookies but behind user choice. First-party data, server-side tracking, tagged links and consent are the measurement layer that survives, and the company should own it, not whoever runs its media.

## [The model is not the product](https://lowob.com/research/the-model-is-not-the-product/)

Published 2026-04-03. Buyers do not pay for a model; they pay for a finished job. Enterprise buyers now run several models at once and say most perform well enough, so positioning on the model makes every pitch sound the same. This piece sets out how to position on the job and workflow, answer the wrapper objection by showing what you own, put every AI claim through a register regulators would recognise, and keep the investor and customer stories apart.

## [CPM, CPC, CPA, CPL, ROAS Explained: Which to Run On](https://lowob.com/research/cpm-cpc-cpa-cpl-roas-explained/)

Published 2026-03-31. CPM, CPC, CPL and CPA describe what a company pays for, and each hides what the next reveals. ROAS flatters, because it counts attributed revenue against media cost alone. The number to manage the business on is customer acquisition cost against value over a realistic horizon, with payback period as the constraint.

## [Build it to run without you](https://lowob.com/research/build-it-to-run-without-you/)

Published 2026-03-27. A GTM system is only an asset if the company owns it: the accounts, the records, the routines and the reasons. Knowledge walks out with people, platforms decide ownership by whose business holds the account, and EU law now backs the right to export from software providers. Build for handover from day one, write handover into any outside scope, and score yourself on ten questions to find and fix the weakest link first.

## [Influencer vs Creator vs KOL vs Ambassador: Definitions](https://lowob.com/research/influencer-creator-kol-ambassador/)

Published 2026-03-25. Influencers sell reach, creators sell content and conversion, KOLs sell authority in a specific domain, and ambassadors sell an ongoing, disclosed relationship. The people may overlap, but the deals should not. Pay each for what they sell, disclose every material connection under FTC and UK ASA rules, and run the whole as a programme.

## [Stop reporting reach](https://lowob.com/research/stop-reporting-reach/)

Published 2026-03-23. Pick the few numbers that show attention turning into money that comes back: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency and source. Report incentivised and organic activity separately, instrument every channel before spending on it, send every audience the same core numbers, and drop vanity metrics from the top of the page.

## [Affiliate vs Partner vs Referral Programs: What's the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-vs-partner-vs-referral/)

Published 2026-03-20. Affiliate programs pay professional publishers a commission per defined event, at scale. Partner programs are fewer, larger deals negotiated company to company. Referral schemes give existing customers small rewards for bringing people they know. Which one a company needs depends on who could plausibly send it a customer, and each needs different terms, tools and measures.

## [Distribution when the platforms are closed](https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-the-platforms-are-closed/)

Published 2026-03-17. Rank channels by the cost of earning a buyer's attention and start where trust is borrowed: partners, referrals, creators and owned media. Sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for your category first, using the platforms' own dated policies. Paid media comes last, once you know what converts.

## [How AI Answer Engines Choose Which Sources to Cite](https://lowob.com/research/how-llms-choose-sources/)

Published 2026-03-17. AI assistants answer from what the model learned in training and from pages they retrieve at the time of the question. Citation studies show the retrieved sources change from day to day and often differ from the pages that rank in search. Content that answers a real question with checkable, sourced facts gives an engine something to use; content written only to persuade rarely does.

## [LLM Optimization Checklist for Content and Marketing](https://lowob.com/research/llm-optimization-checklist/)

Published 2026-03-11. To be cited by AI assistants, answer one real question per page, make claims a reader can check, keep pages crawlable, earn genuine references on sites you do not own, and measure the same questions across several days each month. Google says no special AI markup or llms.txt file is needed; the controlled evidence that exists rewards quotations, figures and cited sources.

## [Your first ten customers are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-customers-are-design-partners/)

Published 2026-03-10. Pick early customers for fit and learning, not logo value. Agree a written success test up front, work closely for six to twelve weeks on the partner's real data, and convert the ones that succeed into paying customers, case studies and references. The research on lead users and on failed AI projects points the same way: the partner with the problem badly and now, and a clear measure of success, is the one that teaches you something.

## [Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned Media Explained](https://lowob.com/research/paid-earned-shared-owned-media/)

Published 2026-03-06. Every channel falls into paid, earned, shared or owned media. Paid is bought, earned is given, shared is borrowed, owned is kept. Research on trust and on publicity versus advertising explains why each does a different job. A working system routes attention from the first three toward owned media, so companies should build the owned layer before rented channels become the whole plan.

## [The first hundred](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-hundred/)

Published 2026-03-04. The first hundred community members are recruited, not attracted. This piece covers the recruitment loop: list 30 names, ask for judgment on a real decision, give the yeses a job, close the loop in public and ask for the next name. Research on online groups shows why each step matters.

## [What Is a Press Release, and When Is It Worth It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-press-release/)

Published 2026-03-02. A press release is a canonical record of an announcement, not a marketing channel and not coverage. Journalists still use PR material, but Cision's 2026 survey found 82% reject pitches as irrelevant and only 22% want more press releases. Issue one when the news is material and citable, write it plainly, and do the pitching separately.

## [Community is a job, not a number](https://lowob.com/research/community-is-a-job-not-a-number/)

Published 2026-02-25. A community earns its keep by doing work the company would otherwise pay for: testing, teaching, referring, building or governing. Decide the job first, design the channel, rituals and recognition around it, and measure contribution to that job instead of member count, which most community teams still lead with.

## [What an Advisor Does for a Web3 Company](https://lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-web3-companies/)

Published 2026-02-25. A useful Web3 advisor helps founders make a few consequential, often irreversible decisions well: sequencing audiences, restraining incentive programmes, judging regulatory posture, finding distribution beyond the crypto timeline, translating for institutions and saying no to an unready launch. In 2026 the rules on disclosure and promotion make the structure matter more: put it in writing, lock the tokens and disclose everything.

## [Run the round like a sales process](https://lowob.com/research/run-the-round-like-a-sales-process/)

Published 2026-02-19. Treat investors as accounts. Pick them for fit, including whether the fund still has capital to deploy, research the partner, get in warm, run first meetings inside a two-to-three-week window, and track every firm through pipeline stages with pass reasons logged. In 2026, with capital concentrated in large, established funds, a fit-first list matters more than a long one.

## [What an Advisor Does for an AI Company](https://lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-ai-companies/)

Published 2026-02-19. An advisor helps an AI company decide, introduces it to the people who matter, and tells it which advantages will not last. This guide sets out the five contributions worth equity, the market benchmarks for structuring the grant (Carta puts median pre-seed advisor equity well under 0.25%), and the requests that turn an advisor into an underpaid, unaccountable employee.

## [Self-Serve vs Managed Desk vs Agency: Who Runs Your Media?](https://lowob.com/research/self-serve-vs-managed-media/)

Published 2026-02-16. Self-serve suits small budgets in welcome categories, if the buyer refuses the platform's defaults. A flat-fee managed desk suits budgets past the fee floor, restricted categories and channels beyond the platforms, and an agency suits large multi-channel spend. Whatever you choose, the accounts, tracking and data stay in your name.

## [Raise against evidence, not narrative](https://lowob.com/research/raise-against-evidence-not-narrative/)

Published 2026-02-12. Investors price risk. Narrative asks them to imagine the risk away, while evidence removes some of it, and in a 2026 market where capital is concentrating in fewer companies, even a small amount of real evidence changes which investors take the call. Keep a dated evidence log, strip out paid-for activity, and put the best evidence on slide 2 or 3.

## [What Is Programmatic Advertising? A Plain-English Guide](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-programmatic-advertising/)

Published 2026-02-10. Programmatic advertising is the buying and selling of ad space by software through real-time auctions. The ANA's 2023 study found only 36 cents of each dollar entering a buying platform reached a consumer. It is cheap, fast and open to restricted categories, but it rewards buyers who set standards and punishes those who do not.

## [One truth, three audiences](https://lowob.com/research/one-truth-three-audiences/)

Published 2026-02-06. Write one product truth, then one belief statement per audience, then a claims register that says what you can prove. The deck, the homepage and community announcements are all derived from those three. The register is also where regulated and AI claims are checked before they ship.

## [Agency Types Explained: Full-Service to Specialist](https://lowob.com/research/agency-types-field-guide/)

Published 2026-02-05. Agencies specialise, and the specialisation determines what you get. The main types are full-service, performance, media, creative, PR and specialist agencies, each paid differently and good at different things. Even large advertisers now do most routine work in-house and buy agencies for capacity and specialist skill. Most small and mid-sized companies need one partner who owns distribution and brings in specialists, not a full-service agency.

## [Agency vs Consultancy vs Advisor vs Fractional: Explained](https://lowob.com/research/agency-vs-consultancy-vs-advisor/)

Published 2026-02-02. Agencies sell execution, consultancies sell answers, advisors sell judgment over time, and fractional executives sell part-time ownership of a function. The names overlap and the markets behind them are moving: fractional titles have more than tripled since 2019 and a fifth of CMOs say AI has cut their reliance on agencies. Match the purchase to what you are missing, and insist on a paid, scoped first step from anyone offering more than one.

## [You don't have three problems](https://lowob.com/research/you-dont-have-three-problems/)

Published 2026-02-02. Fundraising, community and customer acquisition are three outputs of one commercial system. Teams that run them as separate projects pay for the same work three times and end up with a story nobody believes. Start with a named buyer, keep one evidence log, and sequence the raise, the community and the pipeline against each other.
